title:
You are a technical implementation research agent for the Phenotype ecosystem. Research and prototype the feasibility of a **Unified Code Review Surface** that integrates multiple AI review tools.

Current tools: GitHub Copilot (native), GitHub Copilot Autofix (GCA), Cursor agent reviews, CodeRabbit, Forge (local agent via OmniRoute).

Research and deliver:

1. **Integration Architecture**: Design a webhook-based router that receives PR events and dispatches to ONE randomly selected review tool. Show the webhook flow diagram in text.
2. **Persistence Layer**: How to remember which tool was assigned to a PR so follow-up commits use the same tool. (GitHub PR labels, database, in-repo metadata, PR comments)
3. **Rate Limit & Cost Management**: Each tool has different rate limits (Copilot unlimited but throttled, CodeRabbit has monthly limits, Cursor has token limits). Design a rate-limit-aware dispatcher.
4. **Local Forge Runner**: How to run Forge (via OmniRoute main provider-model) as a local review agent on PRs. Show the trigger mechanism (GitHub webhook → local server → Forge agent → PR comment).
5. **Unified Output Format**: Design a common comment format that all tools output to, so users see consistent review comments regardless of backend.
6. **GitHub Checks API Integration**: How to surface the unified review as a GitHub Check (green/yellow/red) rather than spam comments.
7. **Implementation Sketch**: Write a minimal prototype (Python/Node/Rust) that demonstrates: receiving webhook, picking tool, persisting choice, dispatching review, posting result. Can be a simple FastAPI/Express/actix-web app.

Deliver as a technical report with working prototype code and architectural recommendations.

@dataclass
class TokenBucket:
    """Thread-safe token bucket for rate limiting."""

    capacity: float
    refill_rate: float  # tokens per second
    _tokens: float = field(default=0.0, repr=False)
    _last_refill: float = field(default_factory=time.time, repr=False)
    _lock: object = field(default_factory=lambda: object(), repr=False)

    def consume(self, tokens: float = 1.0) -> bool:
        with self._lock:

            self._last_refill = now
            if self._tokens >= tokens:
                self._tokens -= tokens
                return True
            return False

    def time_until_available(self, tokens: float = 1.0) -> float:

            deficit = tokens - self._tokens
            return deficit / self.refill_rate

class UnifiedFormatter:

    @staticmethod
    def from_copilot(raw: dict[str, Any]) -> list[ReviewComment]:
        comments: list[ReviewComment] = []
        for item in raw.get("comments", []):
            comments.append(
                ReviewComment(
                    id=str(item.get("id", uuid.uuid4())),
                    tool=ReviewTool.GITHUB_COPILOT,
                    severity=UnifiedFormatter._map_severity(item.get("severity", "minor")),

                    body=item.get("body", ""),
                    suggestion=item.get("suggestion"),
                    rule_id=item.get("rule_id"),
                    confidence=item.get("confidence", 0.8),
                )
            )
        return comments

    @staticmethod
    def from_gca(raw: dict[str, Any]) -> list[ReviewComment]:
        comments: list[ReviewComment] = []
        for item in raw.get("fixes", []):
            comments.append(
                ReviewComment(
                    id=str(item.get("id", uuid.uuid4())),
                    tool=ReviewTool.GITHUB_COPILOT_AUTOFIX,
                    severity=ReviewSeverity.CRITICAL if item.get("security") else ReviewSeverity.MAJOR,
                    file_path=item.get("path"),
                    line_start=item.get("line"),
                    line_end=item.get("line"),
                    title=item.get("title", "Autofix suggestion"),
                    body=item.get("description", ""),
                    suggestion=item.get("replacement"),
                    rule_id=item.get("rule"),
                    confidence=item.get("confidence", 0.9),
                )
            )
        return comments

    @staticmethod
    def from_coderabbit(raw: dict[str, Any]) -> list[ReviewComment]:
        comments: list[ReviewComment] = []
        for item in raw.get("reviews", []):
            comments.append(
                ReviewComment(
                    id=str(item.get("review_id", uuid.uuid4())),
                    tool=ReviewTool.CODERABBIT,
                    severity=UnifiedFormatter._map_severity(item.get("priority", "minor")),
                    file_path=item.get("file_path"),
                    line_start=item.get("start_line"),
                    line_end=item.get("end_line"),
                    title=item.get("summary", "CodeRabbit review"),
                    body=item.get("details", ""),
                    suggestion=item.get("suggestion"),
                    rule_id=item.get("rule"),
                    confidence=item.get("confidence", 0.75),
                )
            )
        return comments

    @staticmethod
    def from_cursor(raw: dict[str, Any]) -> list[ReviewComment]:
        comments: list[ReviewComment] = []
        for item in raw.get("agent_comments", []):
            comments.append(
                ReviewComment(
                    id=str(item.get("id", uuid.uuid4())),
                    tool=ReviewTool.CURSOR,

                    body=item.get("message", ""),

    @staticmethod
    def from_forge(raw: str) -> list[ReviewComment]:
        """Parse Forge free-text output into structured comments.

        Expects a markdown-ish format with headers like:
        ### File: `src/main.rs` (lines 10-15)
        **Severity:** major
        **Rule:** rust-safety-001
        ... body ...
        ```suggestion
        ...
        ```
        """
        comments: list[ReviewComment] = []
        # Split on file headers
        blocks = re.split(r"(?=###\s+File:\s+`)", raw)
        for block in blocks:
            if not block.strip():
                continue
            path_match = re.search(r"File:\s+`([^`]+)`", block)
            line_match = re.search(r"\(lines?\s+(\d+)(?:-(\d+))?\)", block)
            severity_match = re.search(r"\*\*Severity:\*\*\s*(\w+)", block, re.IGNORECASE)
            rule_match = re.search(r"\*\*Rule:\*\*\s*(\S+)", block)
            suggestion_match = re.search(r"```suggestion\n(.*?)\n```", block, re.DOTALL)

            file_path = path_match.group(1) if path_match else None
            line_start = int(line_match.group(1)) if line_match else None
            line_end = int(line_match.group(2)) if line_match and line_match.group(2) else line_start
            severity = UnifiedFormatter._map_severity(severity_match.group(1) if severity_match else "minor")
            body = block.strip()
            # Heuristic title: first sentence or first line
            title = body.split("\n")[0].replace("###", "").strip()[:80]

            comments.append(
                ReviewComment(
                    id=str(uuid.uuid4()),
                    tool=ReviewTool.FORGE,
                    severity=severity,
                    file_path=file_path,
                    line_start=line_start,
                    line_end=line_end,
                    title=title,
                    body=body,
                    suggestion=suggestion_match.group(1) if suggestion_match else None,
                    rule_id=rule_match.group(1) if rule_match else None,
                    confidence=0.75,
                )
            )
        return comments

    @staticmethod
    def summarize(comments: list[ReviewComment], tool: ReviewTool) -> ReviewSummary:
        severity_counts: dict[str, int] = {"critical": 0, "major": 0, "minor": 0, "informational": 0, "praise": 0}
        for c in comments:
            severity_counts[c.severity.value] = severity_counts.get(c.severity.value, 0) + 1

        if severity_counts["critical"] > 0 or severity_counts["major"] > 3:
            conclusion = "failure"
        elif severity_counts["major"] > 0 or severity_counts["minor"] > 5:
            conclusion = "neutral"
        else:
            conclusion = "success"

        summary_lines = [
            f"## Unified AI Review ({tool.value})",
            f"- **Critical:** {severity_counts['critical']}",
            f"- **Major:** {severity_counts['major']}",
            f"- **Minor:** {severity_counts['minor']}",
            f"- **Informational:** {severity_counts['informational']}",
            f"- **Praise:** {severity_counts['praise']}",
            "",
            "### Comments",
        ]
        for c in comments:
            loc = f"`{c.file_path}:{c.line_start}`" if c.file_path else "general"
            summary_lines.append(f"- **{c.severity.value.upper()}** {loc}: {c.title}")

        return ReviewSummary(
            pr_id="",
            tool=tool,
            comments=comments,
            summary="\n".join(summary_lines),
            stats=severity_counts,
            check_conclusion=conclusion,
            check_status="completed",
        )

    @staticmethod
    def _map_severity(raw: str) -> ReviewSeverity:
        mapping = {
            "critical": ReviewSeverity.CRITICAL,
            "error": ReviewSeverity.CRITICAL,
            "major": ReviewSeverity.MAJOR,
            "warning": ReviewSeverity.MAJOR,
            "minor": ReviewSeverity.MINOR,
            "info": ReviewSeverity.INFORMATIONAL,
            "informational": ReviewSeverity.INFORMATIONAL,
            "praise": ReviewSeverity.PRAISE,
            "positive": ReviewSeverity.PRAISE,

class ReviewDispatcher:
    """Routes PR events to a single AI review tool with rate-limit awareness."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.store = get_store(settings.persistence_backend, settings.database_url)
        self.ratelimit = RateLimitManager(
            copilot_rpm=settings.copilot_rpm,
            gca_rpm=settings.gca_rpm,
            cursor_rpm=settings.cursor_rpm,
            coderabbit_monthly_limit=settings.coderabbit_monthly_limit,
            forge_rpm=settings.forge_rpm,
        )
        self.github = GitHubChecksAPI()
        self.forge = ForgeRunner()

    async def handle_pr_event(self, payload: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Main entrypoint: receive webhook payload, decide tool, dispatch review."""
        action = payload.get("action", "")
        number = payload.get("number", 0)
        repo = payload.get("repository", {})
        pr = payload.get("pull_request", {})
        repo_full_name = repo.get("full_name", "")
        head_sha = pr.get("head", {}).get("sha", "")

        # Skip drafts and closed PRs
        if pr.get("draft", False):
            return {"status": "skipped", "reason": "draft PR"}
        if pr.get("state", "open") != "open":
            return {"status": "skipped", "reason": "PR not open"}

        # Only act on opened or synchronize (new commits pushed)
        if action not in ("opened", "synchronize", "reopened"):
            return {"status": "ignored", "reason": f"action={action}"}

        # Check for existing assignment
        existing = self.store.get_assignment(repo_full_name, number)

        if action == "opened":
            # New PR → pick a fresh tool
            tool = self._select_tool()
            assignment = PRAssignment(
                repo_full_name=repo_full_name,
                pr_number=number,
                tool=tool,
                last_commit_sha=head_sha,
                status="queued",
            )
            self.store.save_assignment(assignment)
            await self._add_label(repo_full_name, number, tool)
        else:
            # Synchronize → reuse assigned tool
            if not existing:
                return {"status": "skipped", "reason": "no existing assignment"}
            tool = existing.tool
            self.store.update_assignment(
                repo_full_name, number, last_commit_sha=head_sha, status="queued"
            )
            assignment = self.store.get_assignment(repo_full_name, number)
            if not assignment:
                return {"status": "error", "reason": "assignment lost"}

        # Fetch diff and files
        diff_text = await self.github.get_diff(repo_full_name, number)
        files = await self.github.get_files(repo_full_name, number)

        # Create GitHub Check Run
        check = await self.github.create_check_run(
            repo_full_name=repo_full_name,
            head_sha=head_sha,
            name=f"{settings.check_name} [{tool.value}]",
            status="in_progress",
        )
        check_run_id = check["id"]
        self.store.update_assignment(repo_full_name, number, check_run_id=check_run_id)

        # Dispatch review asynchronously
        asyncio.create_task(
            self._run_review(
                DispatchRequest(
                    repo_full_name=repo_full_name,
                    pr_number=number,
                    head_sha=head_sha,
                    base_sha=pr.get("base", {}).get("sha", ""),
                    pr_title=pr.get("title", ""),
                    pr_body=pr.get("body", "") or "",
                    tool=tool,
                    diff_text=diff_text,
                    files=files,
                ),
                check_run_id,
            )
        )

        return {
            "status": "queued",
            "repo": repo_full_name,
            "pr": number,
            "tool": tool.value,
            "check_run_id": check_run_id,
        }

    def _select_tool(self) -> ReviewTool:
        """Pick one tool randomly from those currently under rate limit."""
        available = self.ratelimit.get_available_tools()
        if not available:
            # If all are rate-limited, fallback to Forge (local, cheapest)
            return ReviewTool.FORGE
        return random.choice(available)

    async def _run_review(self, req: DispatchRequest, check_run_id: int) -> None:
        """Execute the review and update the GitHub Check."""
        start = asyncio.get_event_loop().time()
        try:
            summary = await self._dispatch_to_tool(req)
            duration_ms = int((asyncio.get_event_loop().time() - start) * 1000)
            summary.duration_ms = duration_ms
            summary.pr_id = f"{req.repo_full_name}#{req.pr_number}"

            # Update check run
            output = self.github.build_output(summary)
            await self.github.update_check_run(
                repo_full_name=req.repo_full_name,
                check_run_id=check_run_id,
                status="completed",
                conclusion=summary.check_conclusion,
                output=output,
            )

            # Also post review comments for line-level feedback
            await self._post_line_comments(req, summary)

            self.store.update_assignment(
                req.repo_full_name,
                req.pr_number,
                status="completed",
            )
        except Exception as exc:
            await self.github.update_check_run(
                repo_full_name=req.repo_full_name,
                check_run_id=check_run_id,
                status="completed",
                conclusion="failure",
                output={
                    "title": f"{settings.check_name} — Error",
                    "summary": f"Review failed: {exc}",
                    "text": str(exc),
                },
            )
            self.store.update_assignment(
                req.repo_full_name,
                req.pr_number,
                status="failed",
            )

    async def _dispatch_to_tool(self, req: DispatchRequest) -> ReviewSummary:
        """Call the actual review backend."""
        if not self.ratelimit.try_acquire(req.tool):
            # Should not happen if selection was correct, but handle gracefully

                tool=req.tool,

            pr_id=f"{req.repo_full_name}#{req.pr_number}",
            tool=req.tool,
            summary="Unknown tool — no review performed.",
            check_conclusion="neutral",
        )

    async def _call_coderabbit(self, req: DispatchRequest) -> list[Any]:

                    "diff": req.diff_text,
                },
            )
            resp.raise_for_status()
            data = resp.json()
        return UnifiedFormatter.from_coderabbit(data)

    async def _call_copilot(self, req: DispatchRequest) -> list[Any]:

@app.post("/webhook/github")
async def github_webhook(
    request: Request,
    x_github_event: str = Header(default=""),
    x_hub_signature_256: str = Header(default=""),
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Receive GitHub PR webhooks and dispatch review."""
    body = await request.body()

    if settings.github_webhook_secret:
        if not GitHubChecksAPI.verify_webhook_signature(
            body, x_hub_signature_256, settings.github_webhook_secret

            raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="Invalid signature")

    if x_github_event not in ("pull_request", "pull_request_review"):
        return {"status": "ignored", "event": x_github_event}

    payload = await request.json()
    action = payload.get("action", "")

    if action not in ("opened", "synchronize", "reopened"):
        return {"status": "ignored", "action": action}

    result = await dispatcher.handle_pr_event(payload)
    return result

) -> dict[str, Any]:

    files = await dispatcher.github.get_files(repo_full_name, pr_number)

    req = DispatchRequest(
        repo_full_name=repo_full_name,
        pr_number=pr_number,
        head_sha=head_sha,
        base_sha=pr.get("base", {}).get("sha", ""),
        pr_title=pr.get("title", ""),

### 1.1 Design Philosophy

The Unified Code Review Surface is a **webhook-based router** that sits between GitHub and multiple AI review backends. It receives PR events, randomly selects **one** review tool per PR, persists that choice, and surfaces results as a single GitHub Check Run.

- **Consistency:** A single assigned reviewer (even if AI) builds context across follow-up commits.

## 2. Persistence Layer

### 2.1 Problem

Once a tool is assigned to a PR, all subsequent commits (`synchronize` events) must use the **same tool** to maintain reviewer continuity and avoid re-introducing the same stylistic comments from a different bot.

### 2.2 Options Evaluated

| Option | Pros | Cons | Verdict |
|--------|------|------|---------|
| **GitHub PR Labels** | Zero infra, visible in UI | 100-label limit per repo; no structured metadata | **Secondary** — used for visibility only |
| **SQLite (local)** | Zero external deps, fast reads | Single-node, no HA | **Primary for prototype** |
| **PostgreSQL / Redis** | HA, shared across instances | Requires infra | **Production recommendation** |
| **PR Comments (in-thread)** | Durable, audit-friendly | Slow, noisy, hard to parse | **Not used** |
| **In-repo metadata file** | Version controlled | Requires write access to repo; merge conflicts | **Not used** |

### 2.3 Implementation

The prototype uses **SQLite** with a simple `pr_assignments` table:

```sql
CREATE TABLE pr_assignments (
    repo_full_name TEXT NOT NULL,
    pr_number INTEGER NOT NULL,
    tool TEXT NOT NULL,
    assigned_at TEXT NOT NULL,
    last_commit_sha TEXT,
    status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending',
    check_run_id INTEGER,
    metadata TEXT,
    PRIMARY KEY (repo_full_name, pr_number)
);
```

On `pull_request.opened`:
1. Randomly select a tool under rate limit.
2. `INSERT OR REPLACE` into `pr_assignments`.
3. Add label `review-{tool}` to the PR for human visibility.

On `pull_request.synchronize`:
1. `SELECT tool FROM pr_assignments WHERE repo = ? AND pr = ?`.
2. Reuse the same tool. Skip if no record found.

## 3. Rate Limit & Cost Management

### 3.1 Tool Limits

| Tool | Limit Type | Default Value | Cost Model |
|------|-----------|---------------|------------|
| GitHub Copilot | Per-user throttling | 60 RPM | Subscription (sunk cost) |
| GCA (Autofix) | Per-org | 30 RPM | Included in Copilot |
| Cursor | Token + API | 20 RPM | Per-seat + API usage |
| CodeRabbit | Monthly quota | 100 reviews/month | SaaS tier |
| Forge (local) | Local LLM / OmniRoute | 10 RPM | OmniRoute quota or local GPU |

### 3.2 Token Bucket Design

Each tool (except CodeRabbit) gets a **token bucket**:

```python
class TokenBucket:
    capacity: float          # max burst
    refill_rate: float       # tokens per second
    _tokens: float
    _last_refill: float
```

CodeRabbit uses a **monthly counter** because it is quota-based rather than rate-based.

### 3.3 Selection Algorithm

```python
def _select_tool(self) -> ReviewTool:
    available = self.ratelimit.get_available_tools()
    if not available:
        return ReviewTool.FORGE  # cheapest fallback
    return random.choice(available)
```

This guarantees:
- **Never exceed a tool's declared rate limit**.
- **Graceful degradation** to Forge if everything is saturated.
- **No cost surprises** — CodeRabbit monthly counter is decremented before dispatch.

## 4. Local Forge Runner

### 4.1 Trigger Mechanism

```
GitHub webhook → FastAPI server
    → Write diff + context to temp prompt file
    → Spawn subprocess: thegent-dispatch --provider forge --prompt <file>
        → thegent-dispatch builds argv for Forge CLI
        → Forge CLI connects to OmniRoute (localhost:20128)
            → OmniRoute routes to the active "main" tier model
        → Forge returns markdown review
    → Parse stdout into Unified Output
    → Post to GitHub Checks API
```

### 4.2 OmniRoute Integration

The Phenotype ecosystem already provides the wiring:
- **OmniRoute** runs at `http://localhost:20128` as the canonical routing framework.
- **thegent-dispatch** (`thegent-dispatch/src/provider.rs:35-49`) knows how to build `forge -p <prompt> -C <cwd>`.
- **dispatch-mcp** (`dispatch-mcp/src/dispatch_mcp/server.py:42-67`) exposes per-tier dispatch tools.

The Forge runner in the prototype uses **direct subprocess invocation** of `thegent-dispatch` for maximum transparency, with a **fallback HTTP path** to OmniRoute's `/v1/chat/completions` for lightweight tasks.

## 5. Unified Output Format

### 5.1 Design Goal

Every backend — Copilot, CodeRabbit, Forge, Cursor — must normalize to a single `ReviewComment` schema so the UI layer and GitHub Checks API integration are backend-agnostic.

### 5.2 Schema

```python
class ReviewComment(BaseModel):
    id: str
    tool: ReviewTool
    severity: ReviewSeverity   # critical | major | minor | informational | praise
    file_path: str | None
    line_start: int | None
    line_end: int | None
    title: str                 # < 80 chars
    body: str                  # markdown
    suggestion: str | None     # code fix
    rule_id: str | None
    confidence: float          # 0.0 - 1.0
    metadata: dict[str, Any]
```

### 5.3 Normalizers

| Backend | Normalizer | Key Mapping |
|---------|-----------|-------------|
| Copilot | `from_copilot()` | `severity` → `severity`, `suggestion` → `suggestion` |
| GCA | `from_gca()` | `security` flag → `critical`, `replacement` → `suggestion` |
| CodeRabbit | `from_coderabbit()` | `priority` → `severity`, `details` → `body` |
| Cursor | `from_cursor()` | `level` → `severity`, `patch` → `suggestion` |
| Forge | `from_forge()` | Regex-parsed markdown headers + `suggestion` blocks |

### 5.4 Summary Generation

The `ReviewSummary` aggregates:
- Severity counts (critical, major, minor, informational, praise)
- Auto-derived `check_conclusion`:
  - `failure` if critical > 0 or major > 3
  - `neutral` if major > 0 or minor > 5
  - `success` otherwise

## 6. GitHub Checks API Integration

### 6.1 Why Checks Instead of Comments?

- **Spam reduction:** One check run per commit instead of N comment threads.
- **Status visibility:** Green/yellow/red directly on the PR listing.
- **Annotations:** Line-level highlights inside the Files tab without cluttering the Conversation tab.
- **Required checks:** Can be configured as a merge gate.

### 6.2 Check Lifecycle

| Event | Check Status | Check Conclusion |
|-------|-------------|------------------|
| PR opened / sync | `in_progress` | `null` |
| Review queued | `in_progress` | `null` |
| Review running | `in_progress` | `null` |
| Review done, no issues | `completed` | `success` |
| Review done, minor issues | `completed` | `neutral` |
| Review done, critical issues | `completed` | `failure` |
| Review errored | `completed` | `failure` |

### 6.3 Annotations

Each `ReviewComment` maps to a GitHub Check annotation:

```python
{
    "path": comment.file_path,
    "start_line": comment.line_start,
    "end_line": comment.line_end,
    "annotation_level": {  # critical → failure, major → warning, minor → notice
        "critical": "failure",
        "major": "warning",
        "minor": "notice",
        "informational": "notice",
        "praise": "notice",
    }[comment.severity],
    "message": comment.title,
    "raw_details": comment.body,
}
```

### 6.4 Secondary PR Review Comments

For actionable feedback (suggestions), the system also posts a **single PR review** (`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}/reviews`) with all line-level comments bundled. This appears in the Conversation tab as one review thread, not N individual comments.

## 8. Architectural Recommendations

### 8.1 Short-Term (Prototype → MVP)

1. **Use SQLite + PR labels** for persistence. No external dependencies.
2. **Start with Forge as the primary backend** — it is free (OmniRoute main tier or local), requires no SaaS API keys, and runs entirely in the Phenotype ecosystem.
3. **Add CodeRabbit as a secondary option** once rate limits and billing are understood.
4. **GitHub Copilot / GCA** should be integrated via GitHub App webhooks (not direct API calls) because Copilot review is event-driven and not exposed as a REST API.

### 8.2 Medium-Term (Production)

1. **Replace SQLite with PostgreSQL** (or Redis for hot cache + Postgres for durable log) to support horizontal scaling.
2. **Implement a weighted selection algorithm** instead of pure random:
   - Weight by historical accuracy (e.g., if Forge has 90% acceptance rate vs CodeRabbit 70%, prefer Forge).
   - Weight by cost (Forge local = $0, CodeRabbit = $0.10/review).
   - Weight by PR size (small PRs → fast/cheap tool, large PRs → thorough tool).
3. **Add a re-review endpoint:** `/dispatch/reevaluate?repo=X&pr=Y` that forces a new tool selection and compares results.
4. **Integrate with OmniRoute's combo routing:** Instead of picking one tool, use OmniRoute's combo system to dispatch a "review tier" that may fan out to multiple models and return the best result.

### 8.3 Long-Term (Ecosystem)

1. **MCP Server:** Expose the review surface as an MCP tool (`run_review`) so any Phenotype agent can request a review programmatically.
2. **Audit Trail:** Store every review result in MinIO / S3 as immutable JSON for compliance and model training.
3. **Self-Healing:** If a tool consistently fails (e.g., Cursor token exhaustion), automatically drain it from the pool and alert via phenotype-ops-mcp.
4. **Cost Dashboard:** Integrate with OmniRoute's analytics dashboard to show per-PR review cost, tool utilization, and acceptance rates.

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|-----------|--------|------------|
| GitHub webhook signature bypass | Low | High | Always verify `X-Hub-Signature-256` with HMAC-SHA256 |
| Rate limit miscount causing 429s | Medium | Medium | Token bucket + conservative defaults; fallback to Forge |
| Forge subprocess hangs | Medium | High | 300s timeout + asyncio cancellation |
| Secrets in PR diff leaked to LLM | Medium | High | Strip diff lines matching `SECRET`/`TOKEN`/`KEY` patterns |
| Check run spam | Low | Medium | One check run per commit; update in-place rather than create new |

## Project Overview

**TracerTM** is an agent-native, multi-view requirements traceability and project management system.

### Stack

| Layer | Technology |
|-------|------------|
| Backend API | Go |
| Python Services | FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, Pydantic |
| Frontend | React 19, TypeScript, TanStack Router, Zustand |
| Relational DB | PostgreSQL 17+ |
| Graph DB | Neo4j 5.0+ |
| Cache | Redis 7+ |
| Messaging | NATS 2.9+ |
| Workflow Engine | Temporal |
| Observability | Prometheus, Loki, Jaeger |

### Architecture

```
frontend/          # React/TypeScript SPA
backend/           # Go API server (separate repo)
src/tracertm/      # Python services & CLI
├── api/           # FastAPI routes
├── services/      # Business logic
├── repositories/  # Data access
├── storage/       # File/markdown handling
├── mcp/           # MCP server tools
├── agent/         # Agent coordination
└── tui/           # Textual TUI
```

```bash
# Install dependencies
task install        # or: uv sync

# Run tests
pytest              # or: task test

pytest -m integration  # integration tests

ruff check . && ruff format .

# Quality gates (full)
task quality
```

```bash
cd frontend

bun run build       # Production build
bun run lint        # ESLint
bun run typecheck   # TypeScript check
bun test            # Vitest tests
```

```bash
go test ./...

golangci-lint run
```

```bash
task dev:tui        # Start all services with interactive TUI
task dev            # Standard dev mode
```
